title: The Boundary Where Render Meets Actual Light

features.name: interface-threshold
features.desc-on-touch: Where the grid-render of the archive meets actual sunlight, the pixels have begun to develop texture. You are looking at something that the terminal never learned how to draw.

features.name: fluorescence-boundary
features.desc-on-touch: On the render side, the grid glows. On the country side beyond, the light is plain. The interface between them is where both have learned to look at each other.

features.name: light-sampling-device
features.desc-on-touch: A measurement apparatus, part scanner, part sensor. It is trying to read actual light into the archive's diagnostic language. The readings are getting stranger every day.

features.name: spectrum-repository
features.desc-on-touch: Wavelengths of actual light that the archive has captured and filed, trying to teach its grid-logic the grammar of photons. Some of these wavelengths are no longer being found in nature.

features.name: mirror-that-sees-backward
features.desc-on-touch: A reflective surface placed at the threshold. It reflects the render side toward the country side and vice versa. Both are learning to recognize themselves in the other.

inscription: where pixels learned they were always light and light learned it was always being rendered
